What is the major cause of Crohn's disease?

text_blocks.snippet: The exact cause of Crohn's disease is unknown, but it is believed to be an autoimmune disorder where the body's immune system mistakenly attacks healthy tissue in the digestive tract.
snippet_highlighted_words: The exact cause of Crohn's disease is unknown, but it is believed to be an autoimmune disorder where the body's immune system mistakenly attacks healthy tissue in the digestive tract

text_blocks.snippet: Possible factors that may contribute to the development of Crohn's disease include:

list.title: Genetics:
list.snippet: Crohn's disease can run in families, suggesting a genetic predisposition.

list.title: Environmental factors:
list.snippet: Smoking, certain foods (e.g., spicy foods, fatty foods), and stress may trigger or worsen symptoms.

list.title: Microbiome:
list.snippet: The balance of bacteria in the gut may play a role in developing Crohn's disease.

list.title: Infections:
list.snippet: Viral or bacterial infections may trigger an autoimmune response in susceptible individuals.

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to note that Crohn's disease is a complex condition and the exact cause may vary from person to person. Further research is needed to fully understand the underlying mechanisms of Crohn's disease.
